dialog.body: Public Works, this is Lorraine. How can I help you?

Hi, Lorraine. Yes, my name is Priya Tran. I'm over at 341 Ayrault Street, up the Historic Hill. I'm calling because of the storm drain out front. After the nor'easter, last weekend, Saturday into Sunday, the water just did not go down.
Okay, Ms. Tran, 341 Ayrault Street. And the drain in front of your house, the water's backing up out of it, or it's just not taking the water?

Both, kind of. It was pooling over the grate and then it ran down the side of the driveway. And, um, I got a few inches in the cellar. A few inches of water, seeped right in along the back wall. I've been in this house a lot of years and that has never happened. Never.
Oh, I'm sorry. A few inches in the cellar, and that's the first time you've seen it.

First time, yes. And I'm worried, because it's still wet down there today. Plus the water's going toward my neighbor's garage. It's running right along the edge of the property and down toward their door. They're not home, I think they go to Florida, so I can't even knock.
Alright. So water's moving toward the neighbor's garage. Is it still running right now, or was that mostly during the storm?
It slowed down but it's still a trickle this morning. Not like Sunday, but it's still there. I don't want it to get in their garage and then it's something else.

Understood. Let me get this down so I have it right. Three forty-one Ayrault Street, storm drain out front not draining since the storm, water in your cellar a few inches, and a trickle heading toward the neighbor's garage. Is that right?
That's it, yes. Exactly.
Is the grate itself blocked, do you know? Leaves, snow, ice, anything sitting on it?
I looked out and there's a lot of leaves and slush packed on it. I thought about going out with a rake, but the street is so slippery, and honestly I'm sixty-some, I don't want to fall in the road.
No, don't go out in the street. That's what we're here for. I'll put in a work order for a crew to come look at that drain and clear it.
Okay. Thank you. Can I ask, do the crews work weekends? Because if it's going to be till Saturday, I'm going to be, well, I'm going to have a lot of water down there.

They do get called in when it's needed, but right after a storm like this they've got a long list. Most likely you'll see someone in the next day or two, midweek at the latest, I'd say. I'll mark it that there's water in a home and heading to a neighboring property, so it gets looked at sooner.
Okay, that helps. I appreciate that.
Is there a number where they can reach you if the crew needs to get a hold of you?

Sure, it's 401-555-0194. That's the landline. I'm here, I'm not going anywhere. And, um, I should say, I may not hear a voicemail right away. A software update on my cell phone ate half my storage, so it's full and it won't take messages. Honestly I don't know what it did. So call the house.
Okay, the landline, 401-555-0194. I'll note to call the house phone and not the cell. Got it.
Perfect. Thank you.

In the meantime, if the water in the cellar gets any deeper, or you see it near any electrical, the panel or outlets, stay away from that and call the fire department's non-emergency line. Don't wade in.
No, the panel's up on the wall, and it's not near that. It's just along the back, by the old shelves. I'll keep an eye on it.

Good. So I've got the work order in for the storm drain at 341 Ayrault Street. Priority noted for the cellar water and the neighbor's garage. Someone should be out in the next couple of days, and they'll call 401-555-0194 if they need anything.
Okay. Thank you, Lorraine. I feel a little better having it written down somewhere.
You're welcome, Ms. Tran. Take care, and stay out of that street.
I will. Bye now.
